translations.text: Since many have undertaken from above to set in order an account of the matters that have been confirmed among us,
just as they taught us, those who from the beginning had been eyewitnesses and servants of the word,
it seemed good to me also, who have followed from the beginning with all truth, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you may understand in truth the words in which you were instructed.
Now in the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
And they were both righteous before the Lord, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of God; they were blameless.
And they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.
And it came to pass during his priesthood, in the appointed order of the days of his service before God,
that according to the custom of the priesthood it fell to him by lot to burn incense; he went into the temple of the Lord.
And the whole multitude was worshipping outside at the hour of incense.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense.
And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
The angel of the Lord said to him: "Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayers have been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
And he will be joy and gladness to you, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before the Lord, and wine and strong drink and [?] he shall not drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
And he will turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

And he himself will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a people prepared."
And Zechariah said to the angel: "How shall I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in days."
The angel answered and said to him: "I am the angel Gabriel, who stand before God, and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day on which this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time."
And the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they were amazed at his delay in the temple.
And when he came out, he could not speak to them, and they understood that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he kept making signs to them, and he remained mute.
And it came to pass, when the days of his service were completed, he went away to his own house.
And after those days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself for five months, and said,
"The Lord has done this for me in the days in which he looked upon me, to take away my reproach among men."
And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city of the Galileans, whose name was Nazareth,
to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the name of the virgin was Mary.
And he came to her and said to her: "Rejoice, joyful one! The Lord is with you!"
And she was troubled at that word, and she pondered: "What kind of greeting is this?"
And the angel said to her: "Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found grace before God.
And behold, you will conceive and bear a son, and you will call his name Jesus.
He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him grace: the throne of David, his father.
And he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end."
And Mary said to the angel: "How will this be, since I do not know a man?"
The angel answered and said to her: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; for that which is to be born is holy and will be called Son of God.
And behold, Elizabeth too, your kinswoman, has conceived in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
For with God nothing is impossible in any word."
And Mary said: "Behold, here I stand, the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word!" And the angel departed from her.
Mary arose in those days and went quickly into the hill country, to the city of Judah.
And she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
And it came to pass, when Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child leapt in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
And she cried out with a loud voice and said: "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For behold, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, this child leapt for joy in my womb.
And blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things spoken to her by the Lord."
And Mary said: "My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit shall rejoice in God, my Savior,
for he has looked upon the lowliness of his handmaid; for behold, from now on all the generations of the earth will call me blessed;
for the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
And his mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear him;
He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts;
he has brought down the mighty from their thrones and lifted up the lowly;
he has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty;
he has helped Israel, his servant, in remembrance of his mercy,
as he spoke to our father Abraham and to his offspring forever.
And Mary stayed with her about three months, and returned to her own house.
And Elizabeth's days for giving birth were fulfilled, and she bore a son.
And her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.
And it came to pass that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they would have called him by the name of his father, Zechariah.
His mother answered and said: "No; rather, he shall be called John."
And they said to her: "There is no one among your relatives who is called by the name John."
They made signs to his father, asking what name he wanted him to be called.
And he asked for a writing tablet and wrote, saying: "John is his name." And they all marveled.
And immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he spoke, blessing God.
And great fear fell upon all who heard this and who lived around them, and all these things were told throughout all the hill country of Judea.
And all who heard laid them up in their hearts, saying: "What then will this child be?" And the hand of the Lord was with him.
And Zechariah, his father, was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
"Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, for he has visited and brought about the redemption of his people,
and has raised up a horn of salvation in the house of David, his servant,
as he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets from of old,
to save us from our enemies and from the hands of all who hate us;
to show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,
the oath that he swore to Abraham, our father, to grant us
that, delivered from the hands of our enemies, without fear
we might serve him in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give his people knowledge of salvation, for the forgiveness of their sins,
through the tender mercy of our God, by which the sun rising from on high has visited us,
to appear to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide us on the way of peace.
And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he lived in the wilderness until the day of his appearance to Israel.
And it came to pass in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered.
This was the first registration of the world, during the governorship of Quirinius over the Syrians.
And everyone went to be registered, each in his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and lineage of David,
to be enrolled together with Mary, who was betrothed to him, and she was pregnant.
And it came to pass, while they were there, that the days of her giving birth were fulfilled.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son, and she wrapped him and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
And there were shepherds in that same place, staying out in the fields, who kept the night watches over their flocks.
And an angel of the Lord stood over them, and the glory of the Lord shone upon them, and they were afraid with great fear.
And the angel said to them: Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy, which will be for all the people:
for today a Savior has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.
And this will be a sign to you: you will find the child wrapped in swaddling cloths, lying in a manger.
And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the hosts of heaven, praising God and saying:
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will among men!

And it came to pass, when the angels had gone up from them into heaven, that the shepherds said to one another: Come, let us go to Bethlehem and see what this thing is that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.
And they came quickly and found Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.
And they remembered the word that had been spoken to them concerning the child.
And all who heard were amazed at the words that the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these words and pondered them in her heart.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them.
And when the eight days until his circumcision were fulfilled, they called his name Jesus, the name he had been called by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord,
as it is written in the law of the Lord: "Every male child that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord,"
and to offer a sacrifice, as it is commanded in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or young pigeons.
And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon, and this man was righteous and God-fearing, and he was waiting for the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Spirit was with him.
And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had seen the Lord's anointed.
And he came in the Spirit into the temple. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him according to the custom of the law,
he took him in his arms and blessed God and said:
"Now, Lord, you let your servant go in peace, according to your word;
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared before the face of all peoples:
a light to shine on the gentiles, and the glory of your people Israel."
And his father and his mother were amazed at the words that were spoken about him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary: "Behold, this child is set for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign of [?] (opposition)."
"And a sword will pass through your own soul, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."
And there was Anna the prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was advanced in many days. She had lived with her husband seven years from her virginity.
And she had been a widow for about eighty-four years. She did not leave the temple, but served with fasting and prayer day and night.
And at that same hour she too stood up and gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke about him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Israel.
And when they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town, Nazareth.
And the child Jesus grew and became strong and was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
And his parents used to go up to Jerusalem every year for the feast of Passover.
And when he was twelve years old, as they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast,
and when they had completed those days and were returning, the boy Jesus went up [?] to Jerusalem, and his parents did not know it;
they supposed that he was with their fellow travellers. And when they had gone a day's journey, they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances;
and when they did not find him, they went back to Jerusalem to search for him.
And after three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
And everyone who heard him was amazed at his wisdom and his answers.
And they saw him and were [?astonished]. And his mother said to him, "Child, why have you done this to us? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in distress."
And he said to them, "Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?"
And they did not understand the word that he spoke to them.
And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart.
And Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature and in favor before God and people.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor over Judea, and Herod was tetrarch over Galilee, and his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch over Abilene,
and in the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of the Lord came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
And he went into all the region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for forgiveness,
as it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, and make his paths straight.
Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low, and the rough places shall become easy, and the stony places straight roads.
And all flesh shall see the salvation of God."
Then he said to the crowds who came out to be baptized by him, "You brood of vipers, who taught you to flee from the wrath to come?
From now on bear fruit worthy of repentance, and no longer say, 'We have Abraham as our father.' I tell you this, that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
For even now the axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
And the crowds asked him, saying, "What then shall we do?"
He answered and said to them, "Whoever has two garments, let him give one to him who has none; and whoever has food, let him do likewise."
Tax collectors also came to him to be baptized, and they said to him, "Teacher, what shall we do?"
And he said, "Do nothing more than what is appointed for you."
Those enrolled as soldiers also asked him, saying, "And what shall we do?" And he said to them, "Do not oppress anyone, do not accuse anyone falsely, and be content with your wages."
And as the people were waiting in expectation, and all were reasoning in their hearts about John, whether he might be the Christ,
he answered them all, saying, "I baptize you with water; one mightier than I is coming, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand; he will clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire."
And with many other things besides he exhorted the people and proclaimed the good news to them.
But Herod the tetrarch, because John rebuked him about Herodias, his brother's wife, and about all the evil that Herod had done,
added this also to all of it, and shut John up in prison.
And it came to pass at the baptism of all the people that Jesus also was baptized, and as he was praying, the heavens were opened,
and the Holy Spirit came down upon him in bodily form, like a dove, and a voice came from heaven and said: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
And Jesus himself was just beginning his thirtieth year. He was supposed to be the son of Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Heli,
son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Jannai, son of Joseph,
son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Nahum, son of Esli, son of Naggai,
son of Maath, son of Mattathias, son of Semein, son of Joseph, son of Judah,
son of Joanan, son of Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, son of Neri,
son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmadam, son of Er,
son of Jesus, son of Eliezer, son of Joram, son of Matthat, son of Levi,
son of Simeon, son of Judah, son of Joseph, son of Jonam, son of Eliakim,
son of Melea, son of Menna, son of Mattatha, son of Nathan, son of David,
son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Salmon, son of Nahshon,
son of Amminadab, son of Aram, son of Admin, son of Arni, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah,
son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor,
son of Serug, son of Reu, son of Peleg, son of Eber, son of Shelah,
son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Lamech,
son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Cainan,
son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.
Then Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and the Spirit led him into the wilderness.
And for forty days he was tempted by the devil, and he ate nothing during those days. And when those days were over, he was hungry.
The devil said to him: "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
Jesus answered and said to him: "It is written: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.'"
And he led him up onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
And he said to him, "I will give you all this authority and their glory, for it has been given to me, and I give it to whomever I wish."
"If you will worship before me, all of it will be yours."
Jesus answered and said to him, "It is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve."
And he brought him to Jerusalem, set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here!"
"For it is written: He has commanded his angels concerning you, to guard you;"
"they will lift you up in their hands, so that you will never strike your foot against a stone."
Jesus answered and said to him, "It is said: You shall not test the Lord your God."
And when the devil had finished every temptation, he departed from him until a certain time.
And Jesus returned in the power of the Holy Spirit to Galilee, and news of him spread through all the surrounding country.
And he himself taught in their synagogues and was glorified by all.
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and as was his custom he went into their synagogue on the Sabbath day, and they gave him the book of the prophet Isaiah.
He stood up and opened the book to read, and found the place where it was written:

"The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the poor, to heal the broken-hearted, to proclaim release to the captives and sight to the blind, to send the crushed away in release,"
"and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord."
And he closed the book, gave it to the attendant, and sat down; and the eyes of the whole assembly were looking at him.
And he began to say to them, "Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
And all bore witness to him and marveled at the words of grace that came out of his mouth, and they said, "Is this not the son of Joseph?"
And he said to them, "Surely you will say this proverb to me: 'Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we have heard was done in Capernaum, do here too, in your homeland!'"
But he said to them, "Amen, I say to you, no prophet is accepted in his own country."
"But I tell you truly, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heavens were shut for three years and six months, when there was a famine over all the land;"
"and Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to Zarephath of Sidon, to a widow woman."
"And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was healed except Naaman the Syrian."
And all who were in the synagogue were filled with anger when they heard this.
And they rose up and drove him out of the city, and brought him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, in order to throw him down.
But he passed through their midst and went away.
And he went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and he was teaching them on the sabbath.
And they were amazed at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
And in their synagogue there was a man who had an unclean spirit, and he cried out with a loud voice:
"Ah, what have I to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? We know who you are: the Holy One of God."
And Jesus rebuked him and said to him: "Be silent, and come out of him!" And the demon threw him down in their midst and came out of him, and did him no harm at all.
And amazement came upon them all, and they talked with one another and said: "What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out."
And the report about him spread through all the places of the surrounding region.
And he rose and left the synagogue and went into the house of Simon. Simon's mother-in-law was gripped by a high fever, and they told him about her.
And he stood over her and rebuked the fever. And it left her at once, and she rose and served him.
And just as the sun was setting, all who had people sick with various kinds of diseases brought them to him, and he laid his hand on each one of them and healed them.
And demons came out of many, crying out and saying: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." And he rebuked them and did not allow them to speak, for they knew that he was the Christ.
And when day came, he went out from there and went to a deserted place. And the crowd looked for him and came to him, and they tried to hold him back so that he would not go away from them.
But he said to them: "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities too, for this is why I was sent."
And he was preaching in all the synagogues of Galilee.
And it happened that, as the crowd was pressing upon him to hear the word of God, he was standing by the shore of the lake of Gennesaret.
And he saw two boats standing at the shore of the lake; the fishermen had got out of the boats and were washing their nets.
And he got into one of the boats, which was Simon's, and told him to put out a little way from the shore. And he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.
And when he had stopped speaking, he said to Simon: "Put out into the deep water and let down your net for a catch."
Simon answered and said to him: "Master, we have toiled all night and caught nothing; but now, at your word, let us let down the net."
And they did this and enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were breaking.
And they signalled to those who were in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they were sinking.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus' knees and said: "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord."
For amazement had seized him and all who were with him at the catch of fish that they had taken.
So also were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. And Jesus said to Simon: "Do not be afraid, Simon! From now on you will be a catcher of men."
And they brought the boat to land, left everything, and followed him.

And it happened, when he entered one of the cities, that there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, saying: "Lord, if you are willing, you are able to heal me."
And he stretched out his hand, touched him and said to him: "I am willing; be cleansed." And immediately the leprosy left him.
And he himself ordered him not to tell anyone, but: "Go and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony."
And the word about him spread all the more, and many people gathered to hear and to be healed of their sicknesses.
But he himself would withdraw into the wilderness and pray.

And it happened on one of the days that he was teaching them. And Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem, and the power of God was there to heal them.
And behold, men were carrying on a bed a man who was paralysed, and they wanted to bring him in and set him before him.
And they could not find a way to bring him in because of the crowd. They went up onto the roof, lifted the man, and let him down with the bed in front of Jesus.
And Jesus saw their faith and said to him: "Man, your sins are forgiven you!"
And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason: "Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who has the power to forgive, except God alone?"
Jesus perceived the thoughts of their hearts, answered and said to them: "Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — he said to the paralysed man: "Get up, take up your bed and go to your home!"
And immediately he got up before them, took up the bed on which he had been lying, and went to his home, glorifying God.
And amazement seized everyone, and they glorified God. And fear fell upon them, and they said: "We have seen the greatest glory today."
And after this he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi at the tax booth, and said to him: "Follow me!"
And he left everything and followed him.
And Levi prepared a great feast for Jesus in his house. And there was a great gathering of tax collectors and of others who were with them, reclining at table [?].
And the Pharisees and their scribes grumbled to his disciples, saying: "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "The living have no need of a physician, but those who are in grievous sickness.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, so that they may repent."
But they said to him: "Why do the disciples of John fast often and make prayers, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but your disciples eat and drink?"
And Jesus said to them: "Surely you cannot make the sons of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?
Days will come when the bridegroom will be taken up from them, and then they will fast in those days."
And he also told them a parable: "No one puts a patch from a new garment on an old garment, lest he tear the new one; and the patch from the new garment will not match the old one.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins, or else the wineskins will burst, the wine will spill out, and the wineskins will be ruined.
Rather, new wine must be poured into new wineskins, and both will be preserved.
And no one who drinks old wine immediately wants new, for he says, "The old is sweeter."
And it happened on the second Sabbath that he was going through the sown fields. His disciples were plucking the heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating them.
But some of the Pharisees said to them, "Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "Have you not even read what David did when he and those with him were hungry,
how he went into the temple of God, ate the bread of the offering, and gave some to those with him as well, which was not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests alone?"
And he said to them, "The Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
And it happened on another Sabbath that Jesus went into their synagogue and was teaching. And there was a man there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and the Pharisees were watching to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find grounds to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts and said to the man whose hand was withered, "Get up and stand here in the middle!" And he got up and stood in the middle.
And Jesus said to them, "I will ask you a question: What is lawful on the Sabbath, to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to kill?"
And he looked around at all of them and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand!" And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, like the other one.
But they were filled with malice and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus.
And it happened in those days that he went out to the mountain apart to pray, and he spent the night in prayer to God.
And when it was day, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles:
Simon, whom he called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot;
and Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became the betrayer.
And he came down with them and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and another very great multitude of people from Judea and Jerusalem and the seacoast, from Tyre and Sidon,
who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases; and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
And all the crowd sought to touch him, for power went out from him, and he healed them all.
And he lifted up his eyes toward his disciples and said, "Blessed are you who are poor in spirit, for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed will you be when people hate you, and when they cast you out and revile you and reject your name as evil, for the sake of the Son of Man.
Rejoice and be glad, for behold, your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same to the prophets.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation.
Woe to you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when all people speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets well in the same way.
But I say to you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
and bless those who curse you, and pray for those who oppress you.
Whoever strikes you on your cheek, offer him the other side as well. And whoever takes your cloak, do not keep back your tunic either.
Give to everyone who asks of you, and do not demand anything back from whoever takes from you.
And as you wish people to do to you, do the same to them yourselves.
And if you love those who love you, what grace is there in that for you? For even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what grace is there in that for you? For even sinners do this.
And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive back, what grace is there in that for you? For even sinners lend to sinners in order to receive back the same amount.
But you, love your enemies, do good and lend, and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he himself is kind even to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, so that you will not be judged; and do not condemn, so that you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, running over, they will give into your lap. For with the same measure you use to measure out to others, it will be measured back to you.
He also told them a parable: "Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is well disciplined will be like his teacher.
Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye, and the beam of the eye [?]
And a certain centurion had a servant who was sick and close to death, and this servant was precious to him.
He heard about Jesus and sent elders of the Jews to him to beg him to come and heal his servant.
Those who came to Jesus pleaded with him earnestly and said to him: "He is worthy for you to do this for him,
for he loves our nation, and he built this synagogue for us."

And Jesus went with them. But when he had come near the house, the centurion sent friends and said to him: "Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under the roof of my house.
That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you either. But say it in a word, and this servant of mine will be healed.
For I too am a man set under authority, and I have soldiers under me. I say to one, 'Go!' and he goes; and to another, 'Come!' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this!' and he does it.
When Jesus heard this, he marveled at his faith. He turned to the crowd and said, "Amen, I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith."
Those who had come went back to his house and found his servant alive.
After this he went to a city called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd went with him.
He came near the gate of the city, and there a dead man was being carried out. He was his mother's only son, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the city was with her.
Jesus saw the woman and had compassion on her, and he said to her, "Do not weep."
He came up to the bier and touched it, and those carrying the bier stood still. He said to him, "I say to you, arise!"
The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother.
Fear fell on all of them, and they glorified God, saying, "A great prophet has risen among us," and, "God has visited his people."
This report about him spread through all Judea and all the surrounding country.
His disciples told John about all these things.
John called two of his disciples and sent them to Jesus, saying, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?"
When the men came to him, they said, "John the Baptist has sent us to you and said, 'Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?'"
At that time he healed many of diseases, afflictions and evil spirits, and he gave sight to many who were blind.

Jesus answered them, "Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind see again, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is proclaimed to the poor.
And blessed is the one who does not stumble on account of me."
When John's messengers had gone, Jesus began to speak to the crowd about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
Then what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who live in fine clothing and luxury are in royal palaces.
Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
For this is the one about whom it is written: 'See, I send my angel ahead of you, who will prepare your ways before you.'
I tell you, among those born of women there is no prophet greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he."
All the people who heard, and the tax collectors, acknowledged that God was just, having been baptized with John's baptism.
But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected God's purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by him.
"To what shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?
They are like children sitting in the streets, who call out to their companions and say, 'We played the pipe for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament for you, and you did not weep.'
For John the Baptist came neither eating nor drinking, and you say: "He has a demon."
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say: "Look, a glutton and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners."
And wisdom was justified by their children.
One of the Pharisees asked him to eat bread with him; and he went into the Pharisee's house and sat down at table.
And there was a woman in that city who was a sinner. She heard that he was in the Pharisee's house, and she brought an alabaster jar of ointment
and stood at his feet, weeping, and began to wet his feet with her tears. She wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said in his heart: "If this man were a prophet, he would know what sort of woman is touching him, for she is a sinner."
Jesus answered and said to him: "Simon, I have something to say to you." And he said to him: "Teacher, speak!"
And he said: "A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
And since they had nothing to pay with, he forgave them both. Now tell me, which of them will love him more?"
Simon answered and said to him: "I suppose the one whom he forgave more." And he said to him: "You have judged rightly."

And he turned to the woman and said to Simon: "Do you see this woman? I came into your house; you did not give me water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You did not give me a kiss, but she, from the time she came in, has not stopped kissing my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed me with ointment.
Therefore I tell you: her many sins are forgiven her, because she loved much. But the one to whom little is forgiven loves little."
And he said to her: "Your sins are forgiven you!"
And those who were reclining at table with him began to say in their hearts: "Who is this who forgives sins?"
He said to the woman: "Your faith has saved you. Go, go in peace!"
And after this he went from city to city and from village to village, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God; and the twelve disciples were with him,
and certain women who had been healed of unclean spirits and infirmities: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, who served him from their means.
And when great crowds were with him, and people came to him from city after city, he spoke to them in a parable:
"A sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell on the road and was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it.
And other seed fell on rock; it sprang up and withered, because there was no depth of soil.
And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up and choked it.
And other seed fell on good ground, and it sprang up and bore fruit a hundredfold. As he said this, he called out: Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!
His disciples asked him: What is this parable?
And he said to them: To you it has been given to know the kingdom of God, but to others it comes in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
Now the parable is this: the seed is the word of God.
Those along the path are the ones who hear, and then the devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy, but these have no root; they believe for a while, and in the time of testing they cast it away.
That which fell among the thorns stands for those who hear the word, and as they go on their way they choke it with the cares and riches and pleasures of this world, and it does not become fruitful.
That on the good ground stands for those who hear the word with a good and noble heart, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed. Instead they set it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, and there is no secret that will not be known and come into the open.
So take heed how you hear. Whoever has, to them more will be given. And whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away from them.
His mother and his brothers came to him, but they could not reach him because of the crowd.
They told him, saying: Your mother and your brothers are standing outside looking for you, and they wish to see you.
And he said to them: My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.
One day he got into a boat with his disciples, and he said to them: Let us cross over to the other side of the lake! And they set out.
As they were sailing in the boat, he fell asleep. A windstorm came down on the sea, and the boat was filling with water, and they were in distress.
They came to him, woke him, and said: Master, we are perishing! He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging of the waters. They ceased, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them: Where is your faith? They were afraid and amazed, and they said to one another: Who is this, that he commands even the winds and the waters, and they obey him?
And they went across to the country of the Gergesenes, which lies across the Jordan [?] and Galilee.
As they went out onto the land, a man from the city came to meet them, who had demons in him. For a long time he had worn no clothes and did not live in a house, but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down at his feet, and said with a loud voice: What is there between me and you, Jesus, Son of God Most High? I beg you, do not torment me.

For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and they would fetter him with chains and bonds and keep him under guard, but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon into the wilderness.
Jesus asked him: What is your name? He said: Legion, because many demons had entered him.
And they begged him not to command them to go down into the abyss.
And there was a large herd of swine there, feeding on the mountain; and they begged him to command them to go into those swine. And he commanded them.
And the demons came out of the man and went into the swine. And the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and were drowned.
When the herdsmen saw this thing, they fled and went and told it in the city and in the villages.
And they came out to see what had happened, and they came to Jesus and saw the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
For those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been saved.
And the whole multitude of the region of the Gergesenes begged him to depart from their borders, for they were seized with great fear. And he went into the boat and returned from there.
And the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might be with him. But he sent him away and said to him:
"Return to your house and tell how much God has done for you." And he went away and proclaimed throughout the whole city what Jesus had done for him.
And when Jesus returned there, the crowd welcomed him, for they were waiting for him.
And behold, a man came whose name was Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue; and he fell at the feet of Jesus and begged him to come into his house.
For he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. And as he went, the crowd pressed in upon him.
And there was a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years, who could not be healed by anyone.
And she came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment. And immediately her flow of blood stopped.
And Jesus said, "Who touched me?" When all denied it, Peter said to him, "Master, the crowds surround you and press upon you, and you say, 'Who touched me?'"
But Jesus said to him, "Someone touched me, for I perceived power gone out from me."

And when the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling and fell down before him, and she told before all the people for what reason she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
And Jesus said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace!"
And while he was still speaking, someone came from the ruler of the synagogue's house and said to him, "Your daughter has died; do not trouble the Teacher."
But when Jesus heard it, he said to him, "Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be saved."
And when he came to the house, he let no one go in with him except Peter, James, and John, and the father and mother of the child.
They were all weeping for her and lamenting. But Jesus said to them, "Do not weep, for the child is not dead, but sleeping."
But they laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
And he put them all out, and took the child by the hand, and called out, "Child, arise!"
And the child's spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. And he commanded that they give her something to eat.
And her father and mother were amazed. But he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.
And he called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons and to cure diseases.
And he sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
And he said to them: "Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bread, no silver, and do not have two garments."
"And whatever house you enter, stay there, and leave from there."
"And wherever they do not receive you, when you leave that city, shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them."
And they went out and went about through the villages, preaching the good news and healing the sick everywhere.
Now Herod the tetrarch heard of the things that were being done by him, and he was perplexed, because some were saying that John the Baptist had risen from the dead.
But some were saying that Elijah had appeared, and others were saying that one of the prophets of old had risen.
But Herod said: "I beheaded John; but who this is about whom I hear such things, I do not know." And he wanted to see him.
And the apostles returned and told Jesus all that they had done. And he took them and withdrew with them privately to a place belonging to a city called Bethsaida.
But the crowd found out and followed him. And he welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those who needed healing.

And when the day began to decline, the disciples came to him and said to him: "Send this crowd away, so that they may go to the surrounding villages and lodge there and buy food for themselves, for here we are in a desert place."
But Jesus said to them: "You give them something to eat." And they said to him: "We have no more than five loaves of bread and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all this people."
For there were about five thousand men. Jesus said to his disciples: "Make those men sit down to eat in groups of fifty."
And they did so, and made them all sit down.
And he took the five loaves and the two fish, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and blessed them, and broke them, and kept giving them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
And they all ate and were satisfied, and what was left over to them of the broken pieces was gathered up: twelve baskets.
And it happened, while he was praying alone, and his disciples were with him, he questioned them and said: "Who do this people think that I am? What do they say about who I am?"
And they answered and said: "John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and some were saying that one of the prophets of old has risen."
And Jesus said to them: "But who do you think that I am?" Peter answered and said: "The Christ of God."
But he sternly warned them and commanded them to tell this to no one.
And he said: "The Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day rise again."
And he said to all: "Whoever wishes to follow me, let him deny himself and take up his cross day by day and follow me."
"For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake, he will find it."
What profit is there for a man if he gains the whole world and destroys himself, or suffers the loss of himself?
Whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed when he comes in his own glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels.
I tell you truly: there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.
And about eight days after these words, Jesus took Peter, James and John and went up the mountain to pray.
And while he was praying, the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing became white and gleaming.
And behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
who appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
But Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; and when they woke up, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

And as they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus: Master, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah. For he did not know what he was saying.
And as he was saying this, behold, a cloud overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
And a voice came out of the cloud: This is my beloved Son; listen to him!
And when this voice had come, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent and in those days told no one anything of what they had seen.
And on the next day, when they came down from the mountain, a great crowd came to meet him.
And behold, a man in the crowd cried out and said: Master, I beg you, look upon my son, for he is my only child.
And an evil spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it throws him down, and he foams [?], and it departs from him with difficulty and crushes him.
And I begged your disciples to drive it out, and they could not.
But Jesus said: O perverse generation! How long am I to be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here to me!
And while he was still coming, the demon threw him down and convulsed him. Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and the boy was healed, and he gave him back to his father.
And all were astonished at the majesty of God, and all were amazed at everything that Jesus was doing. And Jesus said to his disciples:
Let these words sink into your ears, for the Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.
But they did not understand this saying, and it was hidden from them so that they could not grasp it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
A thought also came into them: which of them might be the greatest?
But Jesus knew the thoughts of their hearts, and he brought a child and set him before him
and said: Whoever receives this child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me. For the one who is least among you all, he is great.
John answered and said: Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we were trying to stop him, because he does not follow [?] us.
Jesus said to him: "Do not stop him, for whoever is not our enemy is on our side."
And it came to pass, when the days of his being taken up were being fulfilled, that he himself set his face firmly to go up to Jerusalem.
And he sent messengers ahead of him. And they set out and came to a village of the Samaritans to prepare something for him.
And they did not receive them, because his face was set on going to Jerusalem.
When the disciples James and John saw this, they said to him: "Lord, do you want us to say that fire should come down from heaven and destroy them?"
He turned and rebuked them and said: "Do you not know what spirit you are of?
For the Son of Man did not come to destroy people's souls, but to save them." And they went on to another village.
And it came to pass, as they were going along the road, that someone said to him: "I will follow you wherever you go."
Jesus said to him: "Foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
And to another he said: "Follow me!" And he said: "Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father."
Jesus said to him: "Let the dead bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim the kingdom of God far and wide."
And another also said to him: "I will follow you, Lord, but first allow me to take leave of my household."
Jesus said to him: "No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God."
After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of him into every city and village where they were to go.
And he said to them: "The harvest is great, but the labourers are few. Therefore pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out labourers into his harvest.
Go! Behold, I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
Do not take a purse, or a bag, or sandals, and do not greet anyone on the road.
And whatever house you enter, first say: 'Peace be to this house!'
And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; if not, it will return to you.
Stay in that same house, eating and drinking with them, for the labourer is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house.
And whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you.
And heal the sick in it, and say to them: 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
But whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, as you go out into its streets, say to them:
'Behold, even the dust of your city that clung to our feet we shake off against you; but know this, that the kingdom of God has come near.'
I tell you, it will be more bearable for the people of Sodom on that day than for that city."
Woe to you, Chorazin, and woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
For it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon than for you.
And you, Capernaum, do not be exalted up to heaven; rather, you will go down to hell.
Whoever hears you has heard me; and whoever despises you despises me; and whoever despises me despises the one who sent me.
And the seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name."
Jesus said to them, "I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning.
See, I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice in this, that evil spirits submit to you; rather rejoice that your names are written in heaven."

In that hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, "I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned and have revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was pleasing in your sight.
All things have been given to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him."
And he turned to his disciples privately and said, "Blessed are the eyes that see, and the ears that hear what you hear.
For I tell you: many prophets and kings wished to see and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it."
And behold, a certain lawyer stood up to test him, and said to him, "Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
He said to him, "What is written in the Law? How do you read it?"
And he said, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself."
Jesus said to him, "You have answered rightly. Do this, and you will live."
But he, wishing to justify himself, said to him, "And who is my neighbor?"
Jesus answered and said, "A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and robbers attacked him; they stripped him, wounded him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
A certain priest was going down that road, came upon him, saw him, and passed by.
And likewise a Levite came to the same place, saw him, and passed by.
Then a certain Samaritan was traveling, came to the same place, saw him, and had compassion on him.
He went to him and bound up his wound, pouring on oil and wine; and he set him on his own [?] (mount), brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
And the next day, as he was leaving, he gave two denarii to the innkeeper and said to him, 'Take care of him, and if you spend anything more, I will repay you when I come back.'
Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?"
He said, "The one who showed mercy to him." Jesus said to him, "Go, and you do likewise, and you will live."
And as they went on, he himself entered a certain village. There was a certain woman whose name was Martha, and she brought him into her house.
And she had a sister called Mary, who sat at Jesus' feet and listened to his words.
But Martha was busy and anxious about much serving. She came up to him and said: Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me alone to serve? Tell her to help me.
Jesus answered and said to her: Martha, Martha! You are anxious and troubled about many things; here little is needed.
But Mary has chosen the good fruit, which will never be taken away from her.
And it happened that he himself was praying in a certain place. And when he ceased from prayer, one of the disciples said to him: Lord, teach us prayer, as John taught his disciples.
And he himself said to them: When you pray, say: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done.
Give us our essential bread day by day.
And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive all our debtors, and do not lead us into temptation.
And he said to them: Which of you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight and says to him: Friend, lend me three loaves,
for a friend has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.
And he answers from inside and says: Do not trouble me, for the door is shut and my children are with me in bed; I cannot get up for you.
I tell you: even if he cannot get up and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
And I tell you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Which father among you, then, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him.
And he cast a demon out of a certain man; the demon was deaf. And it happened that when the demon went out, the deaf man spoke. And all the people were amazed.
But some of them said: He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of demons.
And some others, testing him, asked him for a sign from heaven.
But he himself knew their thoughts and said to them: Every kingdom that is divided against itself is laid waste, and house falls upon house.
And if the devil is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say of me that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
If I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves will be your judges.
If I cast out demons by the finger of God, has the kingdom of God not come upon you?
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his goods are in peace.
But when one stronger than he comes upon him and overcomes him, he takes away his armour, in which he trusted, and divides his spoils.
Whoever is not with me is my enemy, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When an unclean spirit goes out of a person, it wanders through waterless places seeking rest, and finding none it says, 'I will return to my house, from which I came out.'
And it comes and finds it swept and adorned.
Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they come and settle in it, and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first.
And it happened that while he was still saying this, a certain woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that you sucked!"
But he said to her, "Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it."
And as the crowd was gathering to him, he began to say to them, "This generation is an evil generation. It seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.

The queen of the South will rise up at the judgement with the people of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgement with that generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah. And behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place, but on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
The lamp of the body is your eye. If your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
See to it, then, that the light in you is not darkness.
If your whole body is full of light and has no part that is dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when a lamp gives you light with its brightness."
And as he was saying this, a certain Pharisee asked him to eat a meal with him; and he went in and sat down at the table.
But when the Pharisee saw this, he was amazed that he had not first washed before the meal.
The Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
Fools! Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
But give as alms what is fitting, and behold, everything is clean for you.
But woe to you, Pharisees! For you take a tithe of mint and rue and every herb, and you pass over justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.
Woe to you, hypocritical Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, and people walk over them without knowing it."
One of the lawyers answered and said to him, "Teacher, in saying this you insult us too."
But he said to him, "Woe to you also, lawyers! For you load people with burdens hard to carry, and you yourselves do not touch the burden with one of your fingers.
Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.
So you bear witness and give your approval to the deeds of your fathers: they killed them, and you build their tombs.
For this reason the Wisdom of God also said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute,'
so that the blood of all the prophets, shed since the beginning of the world, may be required of this generation,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Baruch, who perished between the altar and the temple. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
Woe to you, teachers of the law! For you have hidden the keys of knowledge; you yourselves do not go in, and you hinder those who are going in."
The Lord said these things to them in front of all the people. The scribes and the Pharisees began to plot evil; the word was grievous to them, and they reviled him because of his many words.
And they watched him, to catch some word from his mouth so that they might accuse him.
Meanwhile a crowd of thousands had gathered, so that they were even trampling one another. He began to speak first to his disciples: "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not become known.
Therefore whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have spoken into the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
I tell you, my friends: do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that have nothing more that they can do to you.
But I will show you whom to fear: fear him who, after killing, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is hidden before God.
Even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
I tell you: everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
And whoever denies me before people, I will also deny him before the angels of God.
And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how or with what word you are to answer, or 'What shall we say?'
For the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you are to say."
Someone from the crowd said to him, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."
But he said to him, "Man, who appointed me judge and divider over you?"
And he said to them, "Take care and guard yourselves against all greed, for a person's life does not come from the abundance of his produce."
Then he told them a parable, saying, "The land of a certain rich man was fruitful.
And he considered in his heart and said, 'What shall I do, since I have nowhere to gather this fruit of mine?'
'I will pull down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather there all my fruit and my goods.'
'And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have all good things stored up for many years; rest, eat, drink, and be merry.'
God said to him, 'Fool! This night your soul will be taken from you. And what you have prepared, whose will it be?'
So it is with whoever stores up treasure for himself and does not grow rich toward God.
And he said to his disciples, 'Amen, I tell you: do not worry about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on,
for life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have no storehouse or place to gather into, and yet God feeds them. How much better are you than the birds?
Which of you, then, by worrying can add one cubit to his stature?
If, then, you are not able to do even the least thing?
Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If God so adorns the grass in the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith?
And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be restless,
for all the nations of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows that you need all of them.
Rather, seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give alms. Make for yourselves treasure that does not grow old, unfailing in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your hearts will be also.
Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning.
And be like people who are waiting for their master to return from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.
Blessed are those servants whose master comes and finds them watching like this. Amen, I tell you, he will gird himself, have them sit down, and come and serve them.
And if he comes in the second watch or in the third and finds them so, blessed are they.
But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief would come, he would have kept watch and would not have let the wall of his house be dug through.
You also must be ready, for the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
Peter said to him, 'Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone?'
And the Lord said: Who then is that faithful steward, whom the lord will set over his servants to give them their measure of wheat at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whose lord comes and finds him doing so.
Amen, I tell you, he will set him over many of his possessions.
But suppose that servant says, 'My lord is delaying his coming,' and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
The lord of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him, and at an hour that he does not know, and will cut him in two and put his portion with the unbelievers.
But that servant who knows the will of his lord and does not prepare himself according to his will shall be severely punished.

But the one who did not know, and did something deserving punishment, shall be beaten a little. For from everyone to whom much was given, much will also be sought, and from the one to whom much is given, they will demand even more.
I came to cast fire upon the earth, and what do I wish but that it were already kindled!
But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I came to bring peace upon the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
For from now on there will be five in one house, divided: three against two and two against three.

The father will be separated from the son and the son from the father, the mother from the daughter and the daughter from the mother, the mother-in-law from her son's wife and the daughter-in-law from her mother-in-law.
He also said to the people: When you see a cloud rising, you say at once, 'Rain is coming,' and so it happens.
And when the wind blows from the south, you say, 'There will be scorching heat,' and so it happens.
Hypocrites! You know how to examine the face of the sky and the earth, but how is it that you do not examine this present time?
Or why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For when you go with your adversary before the ruler, make an effort on the way to be set free from him. Otherwise he may drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer put you in prison.
I tell you, you will not get out of there until you have paid even the very last small coin.
At that very time some people came and told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Jesus answered and said to them: Do you think that those Galileans were greater sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered such a thing?
I tell you, no. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
Or those twelve on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think that they alone were debtors more than all the people who live in Jerusalem?
I tell you, no. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
And he told them this parable: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.
And he said to the vinedresser: Look, for three years now I have been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree, and I have found none. Cut it down. Why should it use up the ground for nothing?
But he answered and said to him: "Lord, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put manure on it,
and perhaps it will bear fruit; if not, then cut it down."
And he was teaching them in a synagogue on a Sabbath.
And behold, there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for twelve years; she was bent over and could not look up at all.
Jesus saw her, called her and said to her: "Woman, you are set free from your infirmity."
And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood upright and walked, and she glorified God.

The ruler of the synagogue answered in anger, because Jesus had healed her on the Sabbath, and he said to the people: "There are six days on which it is right to work; come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day."
The Lord answered him and said: "Hypocrites! Does not each one of you untie his ox or his donkey from its manger, lead it away and give it water?
And this woman was a daughter of Abraham, whom the devil had bound, behold, for eighteen years; was it not right for her to be loosed from her bonds on the Sabbath day?"
And as he said this, all his adversaries were put to shame; and all the people rejoiced at all the glorious things that were being done by him.
And the Lord said: "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God, and what is it like?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky made their dwelling in its branches."
Then again he said: "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
The kingdom is like leaven, which a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened."
And he went about through cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
And someone said to him: "Lord, are those who are saved few?" And he said to them:
"Strive to enter through the narrow door. For I tell you, many will seek to enter and will not be able.

Once the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you stand outside and begin to knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, Lord, open to us!', he will answer and say to you: 'I do not know you, where you are from.'
Then you will begin to say: 'We ate and drank before you, and you taught in our streets.'
And he will say to you: 'I do not know you, where you are from; depart from me, all you workers of falsehood!'
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves thrown outside.
And they will come from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south, and will [?] in the kingdom of God.
And behold, there are last who were first, and there are first who were last."
On that day some Pharisees came to Jesus and said to him: "Get out and go away from here, for Herod seeks to kill you."
And he said to them: "Go and tell that fox: 'Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and on the day after I shall be brought to my end.'
But I must go on today and tomorrow and the day after, for it cannot be that a prophet should perish anywhere but in Jerusalem.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who killed the prophets and stoned those who were sent to you! How many times I wanted to gather your children, as a bird gathers its own chicks under its wings, and you did not want it!
Look, your houses are left to you desolate. I tell you: you will not see me from now on until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'
And it happened that when he came to the house of a certain ruler of the Pharisees to eat bread, they were watching him.
And look, there was a certain man in front of him who had dropsy.
Jesus answered and said to the lawyers and the Pharisees: "Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath?"
But they were silent. He brought the man forward, healed him and sent him away.
And he said to them: "Which of you, if his donkey or ox falls into a pit, will not pull it out at once on the sabbath day?"
And they could give him no answer to this.
And he told a parable to those who had been invited, as he noticed how they were choosing the seats of honour, and he said to them:
"When someone invites you to a wedding, do not sit down in the first place at the table, in case someone more honourable than you has been invited,
and the one who invited both you and him comes and says to you, 'Give your place to this man!' Then you will begin, in shame, to take the last place.

But if someone invites you, go and sit down in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, move up higher!' Then you will have honour in front of all who sit at table with you.
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

He also said to the man who had invited him: "When you give a dinner or a supper, do not invite your friends, or your brothers, or your relatives, or your rich neighbours, in case they invite you back in return and that becomes your repayment.
But when you give a dinner, invite the poor, the maimed [?], the lame and the blind,
and you will be blessed, because they have nothing to repay you with, and you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
One of those sitting at table with him heard this and said to him: "Blessed is he who will eat bread in the kingdom of God."
But he said to him: "A certain man gave a great supper and invited many people.
And at the hour of the supper he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited to come, for look, everything is ready.
And they all began, one by one, to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I have no choice but to go out and see it. I beg you, let me be excused.'
And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. I beg you, let me be excused.'
And then another said, 'I have married a wife, and for that reason I cannot come.'

And the servant came and told his lord all of this. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, the strangers, the blind and the lame.'
And the servant said, 'Lord, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.'
And the master said to the servant: Go out onto the roads and the hedges and compel them to come in, so that this house of mine may be filled.
But I tell you: none of those men shall taste of my supper.
And a great crowd was gathering to him. And he turned and said to them:
Whoever comes to me and does not hate his father and his mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and furthermore even his own self, cannot be my disciple.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count how much it will cost, whether he has enough to suffice him until it is completed?
Otherwise he may lay the foundation and be unable to complete it, and all who see him will begin to mock him
and say: This man began to build and was unable to complete it.
Or what king, going to make war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
If not, while the other is still far off, he sends envoys and greets him in peace.
So also every one of you who does not part from all his possessions cannot be my disciple.
Salt is good. But if the salt loses its savour, with what will it be salted?
