It is of use neither for the soil nor for the dung heap; instead they throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And all the tax collectors and sinners were near him.
And the Pharisees were murmuring and saying: This man receives sinners and eats and drinks with them.
And he spoke this parable to them:
What man of you who has a hundred sheep and loses one of them does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
And when he finds it, he puts it on his shoulders with joy.
And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbours and says to them: Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep.
I tell you: in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous who have no need of repentance.
Or what woman who has ten drachmas, that is, satiri [?], and loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search diligently until she finds it?
And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbours and says to them: Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that was lost.
I tell you: in the same way there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.
Then he spoke again and said: A certain man had two sons.
And the younger of them said to his father: Give me my share of the inheritance. And he divided his property between them.
And not many days later the younger son gathered everything together and went to a distant country, and there he squandered his property, for he lived in uncleanness.
And when he had wasted everything he had, a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in need.
And he went to a certain village and attached himself to one of the citizens, and that man sent him into his field to feed pigs.
And he longed to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him anything.
He came to his senses and said: How many of my father's hired workers have more than enough bread, and here I am dying of hunger.
I will get up and go to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
And I am not worthy to be called your child. Treat me as one of your hired workers.

And he got up and came to his father. And while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion, and he got up and ran to meet him, and threw his arms around his neck and kissed him.
And the son said to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am not worthy to be called your son.
The father said to his servants: Bring out the best robe and put it on him; put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet.
And bring the fatted calf and slaughter it, and let us eat and celebrate.
For this son of mine was dead and is alive again; he was lost and has been found. And they began to celebrate.
Now his elder son was in the field. As he was coming and drew near the house, he heard the sound of music and of singers with dancing [?].
He called one of his servants and said to him: What is this?
And he said to him: Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fatted calf, because he was alive and has been found.
He became angry and did not want to go in. And his father came out and pleaded with him.

He answered and said to his father: Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed your commandments; yet you never once gave me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came, who devoured your livelihood with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fatted calf for him.
He said to him: Child, you are always with me, and everything that is mine is yours.
But it was right to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.
And he said to the disciples: There was a certain rich man, and he had a steward. And he was accused before him of squandering his property.
He called him and said to him: What is this I hear about you? Give me an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be my steward.
The steward said in his heart: What shall I do, since my lord is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to labor, and I am ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from this stewardship, people will welcome me into their houses.
And he called in, one by one, each of those who owed anything to his lord. He said to the first: How much do you owe my lord?
And he said: "A hundred measures of oil." And he said to him: "Take your bill, sit down, and quickly write fifty."
Then he said to another: "And how much do you owe?" And he said: "A hundred measures of wheat." And he said to him: "Take your bill, sit down, and write eighty."
And the lord praised that dishonest steward, because he had acted shrewdly. For the children of this world are shrewder in dealing with their own kind than the children of light.
And I say to you: make friends for yourselves by means of dishonest wealth, so that when it runs out, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.
Whoever is faithful in a little is faithful in much; and whoever is dishonest in a little is dishonest in much as well.
So if you have not been found faithful with dishonest mammon, who will entrust you with true wealth?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
No servant can serve two masters, for he will hate the one and love the other, or he will honor the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
When all the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard this, they sneered at him.
And he said to them: "You are the ones who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts. For what is exalted before people is filthy before God.
The law and the prophets lasted until John. Since then the good news of the kingdom of God is proclaimed, and everyone forces their way into it.
But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the law to fall.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
There was a certain rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and feasted splendidly every day.
And there was also a certain poor man named Lazarus, who lay helpless at his gate, covered with sores.
And he longed to fill himself with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table; and even the dogs licked his sores.
And it came to pass that the poor man died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
And in hell, while he was in torment, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
And he cried out and said: "Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am suffering in this flame."
And Abraham said to him: "Child, remember that you received good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus in the same way received bad things. Now, see, he is comforted here, and you are suffering there.
And besides all this, a great chasm lies between us and you, so that anyone who wants to cross over from here to you cannot cross, and no one from there can cross over to us."
And he said: "Then I beg you, O father Abraham, to send him to my father's house.
I have five brothers there. Let him persuade them, so that they do not also come to this place of torment."
And Abraham said: "They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them."
And he said: "No, father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent."
And he said to him: "If they will not listen to Moses and the prophets, even if someone rises from the dead, they will not believe."
He said to his disciples: "It cannot be that stumbling blocks will not come, but woe to the one through whom they come."
It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
[?] Take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times turns back to you and says, 'I repent,' forgive him."
And the apostles said: "Increase our faith!"
And the Lord said: "If you had faith even like a mustard seed, and you said to this fig tree, 'Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,' it would obey you.
Which of you who has a servant who is ploughing or tending sheep will say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Come quickly and recline at table'?
Will he not rather say to him, 'Prepare something for me to eat, and come, gird yourself and serve me while I eat and drink, and then you too may eat and drink'?
Does he owe thanks to that servant because he did all that was commanded?
So you also, when you have done all that was commanded you, say: 'We are worthless servants; we have done what we were obliged to do.'"
And it happened, as he was going to Jerusalem, that he was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
As he was entering a certain village, ten leprous men met him, who stood at a distance,
raised their voices and said: "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
And when he saw them, he said to them: "Go, show yourselves to the priests." And it happened that as they went, they were cleansed at once.
And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back right away and glorified God.
He fell on his face at his feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered and said: "Were not these ten cleansed? Where then are the nine?
For none were found to turn back and give glory to God except this foreigner alone."
And he said to him: "Rise and go! Your faith has saved you."
When the Pharisees asked him when the kingdom of God would come, he answered and said: "The kingdom of God does not come with observation;
nor will they say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'There!' For behold, the kingdom of God is among you."
He also said to the disciples: "The days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
And if they say to you, 'Look, here he is!' or 'There!', do not believe it.
For as the lightning that flashes in the heavens shines out under the sky, so also will the Son of Man be in his day.
But first he must suffer much and be rejected by this generation.
And as it was in the days of Noah, so will it be in the days of the Son of Man:
they ate, they married and were given in marriage, until the day when Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
And likewise, as it was in the days of Lot: they ate and drank, they bought and sold, they planted and built.
But on the day Lot went out from Sodom, fire and brimstone rained from heaven and destroyed them all.
So will it be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, whoever is on the roof, with his goods in the house, let him not come down to take anything; and whoever is out in the field, let him not turn back again.
Remember Lot's wife.
For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses it will save it.
I tell you: two will be in one bed; one will be taken, and the other will be left.
Two will be grinding together; one will be taken, and the other will be left.
And they answered and said to him: "Where, Lord?" And he said to them: "Where the body is, there the eagles will gather."
He also told them a parable, that they ought always to pray and not grow weary in prayer.
And he said: "There was a judge in a certain city who did not fear God and had no shame before men.
And there was a widow in that same city. She kept coming to him and saying to him: 'Give me justice against my adversary.'
And for a while he would not listen to her. But afterwards he said in his heart: 'Even though I do not fear God and have no shame before men,
yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice, so that she will not keep coming and wearing me out.'"
And the Lord said to them: "Hear what the unjust judge says.
And will God not avenge his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night, and is he patient with them?
I tell you, he will avenge them speedily. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find any faith on the earth?"
He told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and who despised others:
"Two men went up to the temple: one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed this: 'God, I thank you that I am not like other men, robbers, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week, and I offer a tenth of all my possessions.'
But the tax collector stood far off and would not even dare to raise his eyes upward, but beat his breast and said: 'Lord, have mercy on me, this sinner.'
I tell you: this man went down to his house justified rather than that Pharisee; for whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
They were bringing children to him so that they might come near to him. And when the disciples saw it, they were hindering them.
But Jesus called them and said to them: Let those children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will not be able to enter it.
And a certain ruler asked him and said: Good teacher, what must I do so that I may inherit eternal life?
Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honour your father and your mother.
But he said: I have kept all these since my youth.
When Jesus heard this, he said to him: You still lack this one thing: sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.
But when he heard this, he became distressed, for he was very rich.
When Jesus saw him, he said: How hard it is for one who has wealth to enter the kingdom of God.
It is easier for a ship's cable to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
But those who heard this said: Then who can be saved?
Jesus answered and said: What is impossible for people is possible for God.
Peter said: Look, we have left everything that was ours and followed you.
He said to them: Amen, I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive many times as much in this present time, and in the age to come eternal life.
And he took the twelve aside and said to them: Look, I am going up to Jerusalem, and everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled:
for he will be handed over to the Gentiles, and they will mock him, and he will be insulted, and they will spit on him,
and they will torment him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise again.
But they did not understand this; that saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was said.
And as they drew near to Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting by the road, begging.
When he heard a crowd passing by, he asked: What is this?
And they told him: Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.
And he cried out and said: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!
And those who were going ahead rebuked him, telling him to be silent. But he cried out all the more, saying: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered that he be called. And when he came near, he asked him:
"What do you want me to do for you?" And he said: "Lord, let my eyes see again."
And Jesus said to him: "See again; your faith has saved you."
And at once he regained his sight, and he followed him, glorifying God. And all the people saw it and praised God.
And he entered Jericho and was passing through it.
And behold, there was a certain man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief of the tax collectors, and he was very rich.
And he wanted to see Jesus, to see who he was, but he could not see him because of the crowd, for he was short in stature.
And he ran on ahead and climbed up a sycamore tree.
And when he came to that place, Jesus looked up and said to him: "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay in your house."
He hurried and came down, and received him with joy.
When everyone saw it, they grumbled and said: "He has gone in to stay with a sinner."
Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord: "Look, Lord, I will give half of my goods to the poor; and if I have falsely accused anyone of anything, I will repay him fourfold."
Jesus said to him: "Today salvation has come to this house, for this man too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man has come to seek out what was lost."
And as the people were listening to this, he went on and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was going to appear at once.
And he said to them: "A certain nobleman went to a distant country to receive royal power for himself and then return.
And he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas, and said to them: 'Trade with this until I come.'
But his citizens hated him and sent envoys after him, and said to him: 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
And on his return, when he had received his royal power, he ordered that the servants to whom he had given the silver be called, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.
And the first came and said: 'Lord, your silver has gained ten more pounds.'
He said to him: 'Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very little, have authority over ten cities.'
And the second came and said: 'Lord, your silver has made five more pounds.'
He said to him too: 'And you, be over five cities.'
And the third came and said: 'Lord, here is your silver, which I kept put away in a cloth,
For I was afraid, because you are a harsh man: you take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.
He said to him: "By your own mouth I will judge you, you faithless servant. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping where I did not sow.
Then why did you not put my silver into trade, so that when I came I could have collected it with interest?"
And he said to those standing before him: "Take it from him and give it to the one who has ten pounds of silver."
And they said to him: "Lord, he has ten pounds."
"But I tell you: to whoever has, more will be given; but from whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
But as for my enemies, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here to me and slaughter them before me."
And when he had said this, he went on ahead of them, going up to Jerusalem.
And it happened that, as he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount that is called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples
and said to them: "Go into that village; as you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it to me.
And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?', say this: 'The Lord needs it.'"
And those who had been sent went off and found it just as he had told them.
And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them: "Why are you untying that colt?"
And they said: "The Lord needs it."
And they brought it to Jesus, threw their garments on the colt, and set him on it.
And as they went along, they spread their garments on the road.
And as they reached the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began joyfully to praise him with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen,
and they said: "Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!"
And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him: "Teacher, rebuke your disciples, so that they will be silent."
But Jesus answered and said to them: "I tell you, even if these were silent, the stones would cry out."
And as he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it
and said: "If only you had known on this day what makes for your peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when the army of your enemies will come up against you, surround you, and hem you in on every side.
They will dash you to the ground, and the children around you will fall, and not one stone will be left upon another within you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation."
And when he entered the temple, he began to drive out those who were selling doves.
And he said to them: "It is written: 'My house shall be a house of prayer,' but you have made it a den of robbers."
And he was there, teaching day by day in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the leaders of the people sought to destroy him.
And they could find nothing that they might do to him, for all the people were devoted to hearing him.
And it happened on one of those days, as he was teaching the people and preaching the gospel in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him together with the elders,
and they spoke to him and said: "Tell us, by what authority do you do these things, or who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "I will ask you one thing, and you tell me:
was the baptism of John from heaven, or from men?"
And they reasoned among themselves, saying: "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
If we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
And they answered and said: "We do not know where it was from."
And Jesus said to them: "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
And he began to speak to them in a parable: "A certain man planted a vineyard and gave it to tenants, and went away for a long time.
And at the proper season he sent his servant to the tenants, so that they would give him some of the fruit. But the tenants beat him, mistreated him, and sent him away empty-handed.
And he went on to send another servant. But they beat him too and sent him away with nothing.
Then again he sent a third. But they seized him, wounded him, and threw him out.
And the lord of the vineyard said: 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.'
But when the tenants saw him, they reasoned among themselves: 'This is the heir; let us kill him, so that the inheritance may be ours.'
And they took him outside the vineyard and killed him. Now what will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others." And when they heard this, they said: "May it never be!"
But he looked at them and said: "What then is this that is written: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner'?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces; and on whomever it falls, it will crush him to dust."
And the chief priests and the scribes wanted to lay their hands on him at that very hour, but they feared the people, for they understood that he had spoken this parable against them.
And they watched him closely and sent spies, deceitful men, who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch him in some word and hand him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
And they asked him, saying: "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach what is right, and you show partiality to no one, but teach the way of God in truth.
Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?"
And he saw through their cunning and said to them, "Why do you test me?
Show me a denarius! Whose image and inscription is on it?" And they answered and said to him, "Caesar's."
And Jesus said to them, "Now then, give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
And they could find nothing to answer in front of the people. And they were amazed at his answer, and they fell silent.
At that time some of the Sadducees, who argue that there is no resurrection, came up to him. They questioned him and said to him,
"Teacher, Moses wrote this for us: if someone's brother dies and has a wife, and he is childless, his brother should marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers among us. The first one married a wife and died childless.
And the second and the third.
And they died childless. It was the same with all seven, and no child was left.
And after them the woman also died.
So then, in the resurrection of the dead, whose wife will she be of them? For all seven had her as wife."
Jesus answered and said to them, "The children of this world marry and are given in marriage;
but those who have been found worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
Nor can they die any more. For [?] David himself says in the book of Psalms: 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool under your feet.'
David himself calls him Lord, so how is he his son?"
And while all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,
"Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in robes, and who like greetings in the streets, and the first seats in the synagogue, and the places of honor at meals,
who devour the houses of widows and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive the greater condemnation."
He looked up and saw the rich people who were putting their offerings into the treasury.
And he saw a poor widow who put in two mites.
And Jesus said, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has offered more than all of them.
For all these offered into this collection out of their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, offered all the living she had."
And some were saying of the temple that it was built with fine and precious stones; and he said,
"Do you see this? The days are coming in which no stone will be left upon another that will not be torn down."
The disciples asked him: "Teacher, when will this be, and what is the sign when it is about to happen?"
And he said to them: "See that you are not led astray. For many will come in my name and say, 'I am he,' and, 'The time has come.' Do not go after them."
"When you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified, for these things must happen, but the end will not come right away."
Then he said to them: "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;"
"and there will be very great earthquakes in place after place, famines and plagues, terrors from heaven, and there will be very great signs."

"But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you. They will hand you over to synagogues and to prison, and they will bring you before kings and rulers for my name's sake."
"And this will become a testimony for you."
"Settle it in your hearts not to rehearse beforehand what answer you will give,"
"for he will give you a mouth and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to withstand or answer."
"For you will be handed over by fathers and mothers, and by brothers and friends and relatives, and they will put some of you to death;"
"and you will be hated by everyone for my name's sake."
"And not a hair of your head will perish for nothing."
"By your endurance you will gain your souls."
"When you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then understand that its desolation has drawn near."
"Then let those who are in Judea flee toward the mountains; let those who are inside the city get out; and let those who are in the countryside not go into it."
"For these are days of vengeance, so that all that is written may be fulfilled."
"But woe to women who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days! For there will be great distress on the earth then, and wrath against this people."
"They will fall by the edge of the sword and be carried off as captives among all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled."
"And there will be signs in the sun and the moon and the stars, and anguish among the nations, bewildered by the roaring as of the sea and its surging;"
"people's souls [?] from fear and from dread of what is coming upon this world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken."
"And then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with power and great glory."
"And when all this begins to happen, look up and raise your hands, for your redemption has drawn near."
"I have longed to eat this Passover with you before my suffering."
"But I tell you: I will not eat of it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
And he took the cup, gave thanks, and said: "Take this and divide it among yourselves."
But I tell you: from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.
And he took bread, gave thanks, broke it, gave it to them and said to them: "This is my body, which is given for you; do this in remembrance of me."
Likewise also the cup after supper, and he said: "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you."
"But behold, the hand of the one who betrays me is with me on the table."
"The Son of Man indeed goes as it has been determined for him, but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!"
And there was also a dispute among them as to which of them was the greatest.
But he said to them: "The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called benefactors."
"But you shall not be so; rather, let the greatest among you be as the youngest, and the leader as one who serves."
"Who is the lord: the one who sits at table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits at table? But I am among you as one who serves."
"You are the ones who have stood by me in my trials."
"And I promise you, just as my Father promised me, a kingdom,"
"that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and that you twelve may sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel."
"Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to have you, to sift you like wheat."
"But I have prayed to my Father for you, that your faith may not fail; and when you have at some time turned back, strengthen your brothers."
But he said to him: "Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death."
But he said: "I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied me three times, saying that you do not know me."
And he said to them: "When I sent you out without purse and bag and sandals, did you lack anything?" And they said: "Nothing."
And then he said: "But now let whoever has a purse take it, and likewise a bag; and whoever has none, let him sell his garment and buy a sword."
"I tell you: this scripture must yet be fulfilled in me, that 'he was reckoned among the lawless'; for what concerns me has its fulfilment."
And they said: "Lord, look, here are two swords." And he said to them: "It is enough."
And he came out from there and went, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples followed him.
And when he came to the place, he said to them: "Pray that you may not enter into temptation."
And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, knelt down, and prayed,
and said: "Father, if you are willing, let this cup pass from me; yet not my will, but let your will be done!"
And he rose from prayer and came to his disciples and found them sleeping from sorrow
And he said to them: "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation."

And while he was still saying this, behold, a crowd came, and the one called Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, was leading them. He came up to Jesus to kiss him, for he had given them this sign, saying: "The one I kiss is the man."
But Jesus said to him: "Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?"
When those who were with him saw what was happening, they said to him: "Lord, shall we strike them down with the sword?"
And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
Jesus answered and said to them: "Let it go this far!" And he touched his ear and healed him.
Jesus said to the chief priests, the captains of the temple and the elders who had come out against him: "You have come out with swords and clubs as if against a robber.
Day after day I was with you in the temple, and you did not lay a hand on me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness."
And when they had seized him, they led him away and brought him into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed at a distance.
And they kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down around it, and Peter also sat down among them.
And a certain servant girl saw him sitting in the light and said: "This man was with him too."
But he denied it and said: "Woman, I do not know him."
And a little later someone else saw him and said to him: "You are one of them too." But Peter said: "Men, I am not one of them."
And when about an hour had passed, someone else kept insisting and saying: "Truly this man was with them too, for he is a Galilean."
But Peter said to him: "Man, I do not know what you are saying." And immediately, while he was still saying this, a cock crowed.
And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said to him: "Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times, saying: 'I do not know him.'"
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
And the men who had seized Jesus mocked him and beat him,
and they said to him: "Prophesy! Who is it that struck you?"
And they said many other blasphemous things against him.
And when day dawned, the elders, the chief priests and the scribes gathered together and brought him up to their council,
and they said to him: "If you are the Christ, tell us." But Jesus said to them: "If I tell you, you will not believe;
and if I ask you, you will not answer me at all, nor let me go.
From now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
And they all said to him: "Are you then the Son of God?" He said to them: "You say that I am."
And they said, "What further need do we have of testimony? We ourselves have heard it from his own mouth."
And their whole multitude rose up and brought him to Pilate.
And they began to accuse him, saying, "We found this man perverting our nation, forbidding the giving of tribute to Caesar, and saying of himself that he is Christ, a king."
And Pilate questioned him and said to him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" He answered him and said, "You have said it."
Pilate said to the chief priests and to the multitude, "I find no fault in this man."
But they were insistent and said, "He stirs up the people and teaches throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place."
When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
And when he learned that he belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, for Herod too was in Jerusalem in those days.
When Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced greatly, for he had long wanted to see him; for a long time he had wanted to see a sign done by him.
He questioned him with many words, but he answered him nothing.
The chief priests and the scribes stood there, vehemently speaking evil against him.
Herod too, with his troops, treated him with contempt and mocked him, and he clothed him in a bright garment and sent him back to Pilate.
And Herod and Pilate became friends that day, for before they had been enemies of one another.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

and said to them, "You brought this man and set him before me as one who perverts the people, and see, I have examined him before you and found no fault in this man concerning the things of which you speak evil against him;
and neither has Herod, for I sent him to him, and now nothing deserving death has been done by him.
I will chastise him and release him."
For it was customary for him to release one to them at each feast.
And the whole multitude cried out, saying, "Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us"—
who had been put in prison for a certain insurrection in the city and for murder.
Then Pilate began to speak again, for he wanted to release him.
But they cried out all the more, saying, "Crucify him!"
And a third time he said to them, "What evil has this man done? I have found no fault in him. I will chastise him and release him."
But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that he be crucified. And their voices and those of the chief priests prevailed.
And Pilate decided that their demand should be carried out.
He released to them Barabbas, the man who had been put in prison for rebellion and murder, the one they had been asking for, and he handed Jesus over to their will.
As they led him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, and they laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
And a great multitude of the people followed him, and of women, who were weeping and lamenting for him.
Jesus turned to them and said to them: "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children,
for the days will come in which they will say: 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nurse!'
At that time they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us!' and to the hills, 'Cover us!'
If they do this to the green wood, what will they do to the dry?"
They were also bringing two other evildoers with him.
When they came near the place called the Skull, there they crucified him and the evildoers, one on the right and one on the left they crucified.
And Jesus said: "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." They divided his garments and cast lots.
And the people stood and watched. But the rulers along with them mocked him and said: "He saved others; let him save himself too, if he is the Son of God, the chosen one."
And the soldiers also mocked him; they would come up before him and offer him vinegar
and say to him: "If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself."
And there was an inscription written over him in Greek and Latin and Hebrew: "This is the King of the Jews."
But one of the evildoers who were hanged reviled him and said to him: "Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us too."
His companion answered in anger and said to him: "Do you not fear God, since you are under the same torment?
For we are justly receiving what we deserve according to our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong."
And he said to Jesus: "Remember me, Lord, when you come in your kingdom."
And Jesus said to him: "Truly I tell you: today you will be with me in paradise."
And it was about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
The sun was darkened, and the court [?] of the temple was torn in two.
And Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said: "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit." When he had said this, he gave up his spirit.
When the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God and said: "Truly this man was righteous."
And all who had come to that sight, and saw what had happened, beat their breasts and turned back.
All his acquaintances stood at a distance, and the women who had followed him from Galilee were watching him.
And behold, there was a man named Joseph, who was one of the chief councillors, a good and righteous man.
He had not agreed with their counsel and their deed. He was from Arimathea, a city of Judea, and he too was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went before Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus,
and he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid it in a tomb hewn out of rock, in which no one had yet been laid.
And that day was Friday, the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was dawning.
And the women who had come with him from Galilee followed after. They saw the tomb and how his body was laid.
They went away and prepared spices and ointment, and on the Sabbath they rested because of the commandment.
But on the first day of the week, very early at dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared, and other women came with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
And they went in, but they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
And while they were perplexed about this, behold, two men appeared in shining garments.
And as they were frightened, they fell on their faces to the ground. The men said to them: "Why do you seek the living one among the dead?
He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he told you while he was still in Galilee,
saying: 'The Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful men, to be crucified, and on the third day rise again.'"
And they remembered his words.
And they returned and told all this to the eleven and to all the others.
Those who told this to the apostles were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them.
But their words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He stooped and looked in, and saw only the linen cloths lying there, and he went away wondering to himself about what had happened.
And behold, on that same day two of them were going to a village about one hundred and sixty stadia from Jerusalem, and its name was Emmaus.
And they were talking with each other about all these things that had happened.
And while they were talking and discussing with each other, Jesus himself came near and went along with them.
But their eyes were held, so that they would not recognize him.
And he said to them: "What are these words that you are exchanging with each other as you walk along the road, and why are you sad?"
One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said to him: "Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there in these days?"
And he said to them: "What things?" And they said to him: "Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a man, a prophet, mighty in deed and word before God and all the people;
how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to the sentence of death and crucified him.
And we were hoping that he was the one who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, this is the third day since it happened.
But also certain women from among us amazed us, who went early at dawn to the tomb
and did not find his body. They came and were saying: 'We have seen a vision of angels, who were saying that he is alive.'
And some of us also went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see."
And he said to them: "O foolish ones, and slow to believe all that the prophets spoke!
Was it not necessary in every way for the Christ to suffer and to enter into his glory?"
And beginning from Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them from all the scriptures the things that are written about him.
As they drew near to the village to which they were going, he made as if to go farther.
And they urged him and said to him: "Stay with us, for it is evening and the sun has declined." And he went in to stay with them.
And it came to pass, as he reclined at table with them, he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
And their eyes were opened and they recognized him. And he vanished from them.
And they said to one another: "Were not our hearts burning while he was speaking to us and as he was explaining the scriptures to us?"
And they rose up that same hour and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
who told them: "The Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon."
And they recounted to them what had happened on the road, and how he had been made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
While they were still saying this, Jesus himself stood among them and said to them: "My peace be with you! It is I; do not be afraid!"
They were startled and frightened, thinking that they were seeing some apparition.
And he said: "Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
See my hands and my feet, that I am the very same. Touch me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have."
And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
And while they still disbelieved for joy and were marvelling, he said to them: "Do you have anything here to eat?"
And they gave him a piece of roasted fish and a honeycomb.
And he took it and ate before them, and gave the rest to them.
And he said to them: "These are the words that I spoke to you while I was with you: that everything written about me in the law of Moses, in the prophets and in the psalms must be fulfilled."
Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures,
and he said to them: "Thus it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day,
and for repentance and the forgiveness of sins to be preached in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
And you are witnesses of all this.
And behold, I am sending the promise of my Father upon you. And you, stay in this city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high."
He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
And it came to pass that, while he was blessing them, he parted from them.
And they worshipped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they were continually in the temple, blessing God.
